questions.text: National ID System Uptime: Critical infrastructure availability: (1) Uptime of ID verification API (for banks/telcos); (2) Redundancy of central database; (3) Disaster recovery capability (off-site backup); (4) Impact of downtime on economy; (5) Maintenance window scheduling; (6) DDoS protection; (7) SLA with private sector verifiers.
questions.evidence_required: API uptime logs, Disaster recovery plan, Incident reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: When ID system goes down, SIM registration and banking stops. It is a single point of failure for the digital economy.

questions.text: e-Government Portal Reliability: Service delivery uptime: (1) Portal availability (e.g., e-Citizen); (2) Payment gateway reliability; (3) Load handling (e.g., tax filing deadline spikes); (4) Mobile app stability; (5) Browser compatibility; (6) Error rate during submission; (7) Receipt generation reliability.
questions.evidence_required: Portal uptime stats, Payment failure rates, Load test results
questions.africa_specific_notes: Portals often crash during deadlines (e.g., tax returns). Payment failures leave citizens with money deducted but no service.

questions.text: Biometric Accuracy & Failure Rates: Ensuring inclusion: (1) False Rejection Rate (FRR) for manual laborers/elderly; (2) False Acceptance Rate (FAR); (3) Multi-modal capability (Iris/Face if fingerprints fail); (4) Exception handling process (for amputees/unreadable prints); (5) De-duplication accuracy (ABIS performance); (6) Latency of matching; (7) Spoof detection (liveness check).
questions.evidence_required: Biometric performance report (FRR/FAR), Exception logs, ABIS test results
questions.africa_specific_notes: Manual laborers often have worn fingerprints. High FRR leads to exclusion from voting/benefits. Exception handling is often missing.

questions.text: Data Registry Integrity: Clean records: (1) Prevention of 'Ghost Workers' (payroll); (2) Prevention of duplicate IDs; (3) Deceased person management (updating death registry); (4) Audit trail of record changes; (5) Data cleansing frequency; (6) Integration between Civil Reg and ID; (7) Historical record preservation.
questions.evidence_required: Data audit reports, De-duplication stats, Ghost worker purge reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Ghost workers are a massive drain on public funds. Dead voters often remain on rolls. Linking birth/death to ID is a challenge.

questions.text: Offline Registration Capability: Reaching the last mile: (1) Kit battery life; (2) Store-and-forward capability (sync when online); (3) Data encryption on device (if lost); (4) Ruggedness of kits; (5) Solar charging options; (6) GPS tagging of registration; (7) Sync conflict resolution.
questions.evidence_required: Kit specs, Field test reports, Sync logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Registration often happens in villages without power/net. Kits must store data securely for days before syncing.

questions.text: Connectivity & Hosting Infrastructure: Backend resilience: (1) Data center tier (Tier 3?); (2) Local hosting (sovereignty); (3) Bandwidth capacity for government WAN; (4) Power backup for data centers; (5) Cloud strategy (Private vs Public); (6) Network redundancy; (7) Hardware lifecycle management.
questions.evidence_required: Data center audit, Network topology, Hosting contracts
questions.africa_specific_notes: Government data centers often poorly maintained. 'Sovereign cloud' is a growing trend to keep data in-country.

questions.text: Cybersecurity & Breach Prevention: Protecting national data: (1) Encryption at rest and in transit; (2) Access control (PKI/MFA for officials); (3) SOC (Security Operations Center) monitoring; (4) Penetration testing frequency; (5) Insider threat monitoring; (6) Patch management; (7) Supply chain security (hardware backdoors).
questions.evidence_required: Pen test reports, SOC logs, Encryption policy
questions.africa_specific_notes: ID databases are high-value targets. Insider threat (selling data) is high. Hardware often imported from nations with geopolitical interests.

questions.text: Identity Credential Security: Preventing forgery: (1) Smart card security features (chip/hologram); (2) Digital signature on QR codes; (3) Mobile ID security (TEE/SE); (4) Revocation mechanism (CRL); (5) Anti-cloning measures; (6) Secure issuance process; (7) Verification API security.
questions.evidence_required: Card specs, Security feature documentation, Revocation logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Fake IDs facilitate crime/terrorism. Verifiable credentials (QR codes) are replacing plastic cards in some areas.

scoring_notes: Layer 1 (Reliability) for Government in SSA: The ID system is the 'root of trust' for the nation. If it fails or excludes people (biometrics), the social contract breaks.
